rationale.conceptual: The agent must understand how to load and use a pre-trained AP-Net2 model to extract penultimate-layer embeddings, then design and train delta-ML feedforward networks for five specific quantum chemical levels of theory. This is a non-trivial task requiring integration of a custom message-passing network with standard deep learning, plus domain-specific dataset handling. It is an established but multi-component documented method, not a textbook operation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of data preparation, embedding extraction, training 5 baseline delta-models, evaluating MAE, training 25 all-to-all models, and clustering. That is 6 sequential stages with dependencies and two distinct scored deliverables. Handling the external dataset and pre-trained model, managing the training loops, and ensuring correct output formats add moderate execution complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a published delta-ML pipeline: extracting embeddings from a pre-trained neural network (AP-Net2), training several feedforward networks, performing all-to-all training, and hierarchical clustering. While the core methods are not novel, integrating the custom pre-trained model and handling the multi-stage workflow with specific output schemas poses moderate difficulty. The conceptual challenge is a 3 (multi-part algorithm needing careful integration), and the execution challenge is a 3 (4–6 stage pipeline with dependency on loading a pre-trained model). Resources are modest: the models are small and trained on a few thousand dimers; all work can be done on CPU with minimal memory.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The full paper used 8-core CPUs for all 80-method all-to-all training (450 walltime hours). The reduced task trains only 30 small feedforward networks on a 3324-dimer subset; the AP-Net2 embedding extraction and FFN training are lightweight, requiring only a multi-core CPU and a few GB of RAM, no GPU.
